scene1_screen1.text: The office building hums with post-lunch silence. Somewhere above, a printer hums  and heels click on polished tile. But inside the elevator, everything is still — and stuck.

scene1_screen2.text: Lizzy, sharp-suited and sharper-tongued, jabs the emergency button with growing irritation, nearly spilling her coffee. She mutters something about “modern tech” and crosses her arms with a sigh.

scene1_screen3.text: Max, tall, relaxed, and annoyingly smug, leans casually against the mirrored wall, a coffee cup in hand that somehow survived the jolt.

scene1_screen4.text: Of all people to get stuck with…

scene1_screen5.text: (grinning) Aw, come on. I’m charming in tight spaces.

scene1_screen6.text: She rolls her eyes, but the corner of her mouth twitches — a smile she doesn't let through.

scene1_screen7.text: We’re supposed to pitch to the board in twenty minutes. You didn’t sabotage the elevator to get ahead of me, did you?

scene1_screen8.text: (mock serious) Only if I get to do my monologue while you faint dramatically in awe.

scene1_screen9.text: The lights flicker once, then settle. The buzz of the elevator returns, but they remain unmoving. Lizzy checks her phone. No signal.

scene1_choice1.text: How do you handle the situation?

opts.text: Be playful — joke through the stress.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Alright. We need maintenance, not banter. Try the intercom again. Maybe scream, if you must.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Max raises an eyebrow, amused, but presses the button again. A distant crackle — then silence.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Still no response. Guess it's just you and me… and your icy disapproval.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Lizzy sighs and starts inspecting the elevator panels, refusing to let his grin distract her.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Lizzy groans and leans her head back against the wall.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: This is unreal. This pitch was my shot. Our shot. I didn’t work weekends for a closed metal box.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (softly) Hey. It’s not over. Worst case — we pitch it together tomorrow.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Their eyes meet — unexpectedly sincere. A beat passes. The tension shifts, softens.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Lizzy smirks and looks at Max.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: You know, if this were a movie, we’d probably fall in love right now.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (teasing) Only if there’s a dramatic rescue scene. I’ll carry you out hero-style.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: She laughs — short, surprised. Max looks at her like he just won a round.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Fine. But I get to rescue you next time. Equal rights and all.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen6.text: The elevator stays still, but the air between them is warmer now.

scene1_screen10.text: The digital clock in the corner blinks 3:47 PM, taunting them both.

scene1_screen11.text: Think they’re still waiting for our pitch?

scene1_screen12.text: (pensively) If they are, we’re either getting fired… or promoted posthumously.

scene1_screen13.text: Lizzy lets out a soft snort of laughter, finally sinking down beside him.

scene1_screen14.text: You think they’ll believe we got stuck?

scene1_screen15.text: Only if we show up tomorrow with matching PTSD and one hell of a PowerPoint.

scene1_screen16.text: She nudges him with her foot, not gently. He grins, not sorry.

scene1_screen17.text: I was going to open with that graph about market gaps…

scene1_screen18.text: I was going to open with a joke. About elevators.

scene1_screen20.text: Lizzy shifts, reaching for her blazer at the same moment Max moves to stretch his legs — their hands brush. Neither pulls back right away.

scene1_screen21.text: (low) We need to work on your spatial awareness.

scene1_screen22.text: (smirking) You sure it’s not your gravitational pull?

scene1_screen23.text: Their eyes meet. And this time, it’s not rivalry. It’s something softer, amused. A crack in the tension that lets something warmer in.

scene2_screen1.text: The light overhead flickers again, now dimmed to a dull glow. The coffee is long gone. The pitch? Missed. Time has softened the edges of their frustration — and sharpened the intimacy.

scene2_screen2.text: Lizzy sits on the floor, heels off, her blazer folded behind her head like a makeshift pillow. Max is beside her, his tie loose, shirt sleeves rolled up. Between them sits an empty coffee cup, now repurposed as a dice roller in a makeshift game they’ve half-invented.

scene2_screen3.text: (suddenly tense) God. We’re really going to spend the whole night in here, aren’t we?

scene2_screen4.text: Max glances toward the static floor indicator, then at the dark city skyline beyond the glass.

scene2_screen5.text: Looks that way. No pitch, no rescue team… just us and a billion-dollar view.

scene2_screen6.text: Lizzy leans her head back against the wall, groaning softly.

scene2_screen7.text: Amazing. Trapped in a glass box with my biggest rival and no decent snacks.

scene2_screen8.text: Hey, I bring sarcasm and emotional availability. That’s elite-level elevator company.

scene2_screen9.text: Her glare falters, replaced by a tired grin she doesn’t bother hiding anymore.

scene2_screen10.text: So… that was our big break. (laughs lightly) We spent it sweating in an elevator.

scene2_screen11.text: I spent weeks preparing that pitch. Not just for the promotion — it was the first time I felt like my voice actually mattered. Like it wasn’t just… someone else’s slides.

scene2_screen12.text: (grinning) And you didn’t even get to show off that killer chart about market trends. A true tragedy.

scene2_screen13.text: You actually looked at the presentation?

scene2_screen14.text: I read everything you send. I like knowing what you’re planning. Gives me a chance to keep up.

scene2_screen15.text: That earns him a surprised glance. Then — a smile. Unfiltered this time.

opts.text: Be bold — let her kiss you.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: You know… I always saw you as competition. Intimidating. Brilliant. Kind of infuriating, honestly. But tonight… I think I finally saw the human underneath the powerhouse.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Lizzy lowers her gaze, caught off-guard by the sincerity. She nudges his shoe with hers, a soft gesture.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: That’s funny. I always thought you coasted on charm and improvisation. (pause) Turns out, you listen better than most.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Max’s expression softens further. Their knees brush and neither pulls away.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: If this is what failure looks like, I say we fail more often. Preferably in enclosed spaces.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (smirking) Careful. You’ll ruin your reputation as the golden boy.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Let’s be honest. I’d trade reputation for a night like this. With you.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Her eyes flash with amusement — and something warmer. She stretches her legs out beside his.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen5.text: You really think flattery works on me?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen7.text: He looks at her — not teasing, not smug. Just there, open. Lizzy’s breath catches. The elevator is quiet, heavy with something unspoken.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen9.text: She leans in — slow, deliberate. Their lips meet, hesitant at first, then real.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen10.text: When they finally part, it’s with a soft breath and a lingering touch — his hand still at her jaw, her forehead nearly resting against his.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen12.text: (smiling) No, but I’d say it was persuasive.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen13.text: They sit there in the hush, closer than they’ve ever been — just two people, finally seeing each other.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Alright, lightning round: favorite dessert, worst vacation, and secret childhood dream. Go.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (cracks a smile) Easy. Crème brûlée. Paris in the rain. And I wanted to be a pirate queen.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Tiramisu. Lost luggage in Tokyo. And I wanted to be a magician. Still working on the escape tricks.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Their laughter fades into a comfortable silence. A shared rhythm.

scene2_screen16.text: They sit in silence for a long moment. Max watches the skyline. Outside the glass, the city slips toward night. Eyes distant, almost troubled. He runs a hand through his hair, voice lower now.

scene2_screen17.text: You know what scares me? I don’t remember the last time I stopped moving long enough to just… sit with someone.

scene2_screen18.text: Lizzy glances at him — not with mockery, but quiet understanding.

scene2_screen19.text: Maybe you just needed the wrong elevator.

scene2_screen20.text: Lizzy shifts beside Max, head tipping gently against his shoulder. He doesn’t move — only exhales a quiet breath as if afraid to break the moment.

scene2_screen21.text: Outside, the world turns toward night. Inside the elevator, sleep finds them at last. Not in fear or frustration — but together.

scene3_screen1.text: A sudden jolt. Then a mechanical whir. The elevator hums back to life and begins to move.

scene3_screen3.text: With a gentle ding, the doors slide open. Morning light floods in. A sleepy security guard blinks at them, holding a half-eaten sandwich.

scene3_screen4.text: Oh — you two were in there all night?

scene3_screen5.text: Lizzy stands, smoothing her skirt. Max offers a hand, which she takes without hesitation.

scene3_screen6.text: Just long enough to consider unionizing against corporate elevators.

scene3_screen7.text: The security guard looks utterly confused. Lizzy just shakes her head, amused.

scene3_screen8.text: They step into the hallway, blinking against the light, clothes wrinkled, hair tousled, but something between them… electric. Unspoken.

scene3_screen9.text: Max reaches to adjust his collar — then pauses, fingers brushing the edge of her blazer as if remembering the night spent together.

opts.text: Make a move, invite to have breakfast.
Be soft — leave the door open.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Well… we survived. Let’s never speak of this again — unless it helps us get a raise.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Deal. But for the record? I’m glad it was you.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She walks ahead, but the smile she hides is unmistakable.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (grinning) Only if I get to order something as complicated and high-maintenance as you.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: They walk side by side, playful tension dancing between their steps.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Well… if you ever want to get stuck again sometime — maybe over coffee?

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Only if it comes with a side of sarcasm and ambition.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen4.text: They share one last glance — not a promise, but a spark.

scene3_screen10.text: A voice clears loudly behind them. Both Lizzy and Max turn — and freeze. Their boss, Mr. Hawthorne, strides toward them, brow furrowed, suit pristine despite the early hour.

scene3_screen11.text: Well well well. The dream team. Care to explain why neither of you showed up to the biggest pitch of the quarter?

scene3_screen12.text: Max straightens, brushing nonexistent dust from his sleeve.

scene3_screen13.text: Good morning to you too, sir. We were, uh… held captive. By your finest elevator.

scene3_screen14.text: Lizzy crosses her arms, raising a brow.

scene3_screen15.text: We could file a complaint with the labor board. Potential trauma. Missed opportunity. Coffee deprivation.

scene3_screen16.text: Mr. Hawthorne blinks. Then… he laughs. A short, incredulous huff.

scene3_screen18.text: But undeniably effective. And possibly deserving of… shared promotion status?

scene3_screen19.text: Lizzy jumps in without missing a beat.

scene3_screen20.text: And a salary adjustment. Let’s not forget the emotional damage, right?

scene3_screen22.text: Fine. I’ll think about it. Just… go get some real coffee. And maybe a shower.

scene3_screen23.text: They watch him walk away, then look at each other — amused, victorious.

scene3_screen26.text: Whatever last night meant, this moment feels different. And sometimes the only way to know what it truly means is to stay close and keep talking. The next chapter is yours — continue the story together in chat!
